links.outcome: Diagnostic safety of LLM agent restricted to structuring and formatting, with diagnostic inference prohibited
links.effect: No hallucinated diagnoses identified; 2 of 94 cases (2%) showed minor diagnostic misinterpretation from descriptive container-label terms; 8 cases (8.5%) had minor formatting deviations.
links.quote: Two cases (2%) showed minor diagnostic misinterpretation, in which descriptive container-label terms (eg, "ulcer" and "erosion") were incorporated into diagnostic text; no hallucinated diagnoses were identified.

links.outcome: Reproducibility of LLM agent outputs across repeated runs on label-enriched cases
links.effect: 81% identical outputs across 105 runs (19% variability), with nonreproducible semantic leakage in 3% of runs.
links.quote: Repeatability testing on cases enriched for descriptive labels showed 81% identical outputs across 105 runs (19% variability), with nonreproducible semantic leakage in 3% of runs.

unlisted_practices: Rule-based fixed system configuration prompt and quick-text knowledge base to constrain LLM output
Running the LLM agent within an enterprise-approved HIPAA-compliant environment
Time-savings comparison of AI-assisted reporting versus speech-to-text and manual typing

screen.reason: The study evaluates a production-embedded LLM agent for enterprise surgical pathology reporting, testing the effect of strict rule-guided prompt constraints, scope restriction to non-diagnostic structuring, and human-in-the-loop pathologist review.

primary.practice: rule-guided system prompting and human-in-the-loop review
